test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following rulers is NOT the part of the Kadai Yelu Vallalgal (The Seven Great Patrons)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nediyon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kadai Yelu Vallalgal**, also known as the **Seven Last Patrons** of the **Sangam Era**, were celebrated chieftains known for their extraordinary **philanthropy** and support for **Tamil poets**.
 
• The seven patrons include **Pari**, **Pegan**, **Kari**, **Ay**, **Adiyaman**, **Nalli**, and **Ory**. They were independent rulers of hilly regions who prioritized welfare and art over territorial expansion.
 
• **Nediyon** is not part of this specific group. The name **Nediyon** is often associated with the early **Pandyan Dynasty** kings, specifically **Nilantharu Thiruvir Pandyan**, or used as a poetic reference to a tall, primordial king in **Tamil literature**.
 
• While the **Seven Patrons** belonged to the **Sangam Age** (roughly 300 BCE to 300 CE), **Nediyon** represents a different historical or mythical lineage of the **Pandyan** kingdom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The specific acts of generosity by the other options are as follows:
 
 
• **Pari**: The ruler of **Parambu Nadu**, he is famous for leaving his royal chariot for a **Mullai** (jasmine) creeper to climb when he saw it lacked support.
 
• **Adiyaman**: Also known as **Adiyaman Neduman Anchi** of **Tagadur**, he gifted a rare, immortality-granting **Black Gooseberry (Nelli)** to the renowned poetess **Avvaiyar**.
 
• **Pegan**: The chieftain of the **Aavi** tribe in the **Palani Hills**, he was moved by a shivering **peacock** and covered it with his expensive silk shawl.
 
• **Valvil Ory**: Ruler of the **Kolli Hills**, known for his archery skills and his patronage of the **Paanars** (musical bards).
 
• **Malaiyaman Thirumudi Kari**: Chieftain of **Mullur**, celebrated for his bravery and for donating his horses and land.
